candidate.answerReason: The trip lasts 15 minutes, during which 150 gallons enter. Removing at least 120 gallons requires 8 gallons per minute, and this rate keeps the retained water at or below 30 gallons throughout.

methods.label: Budget the water during the trip
methods.explanation:
First find how long LeRoy must keep the boat afloat. Rowing \(1\) mile at \(4\) miles per hour takes
\[
\frac14\text{ hour}=15\text{ minutes}.
\]
During that time, \(10\cdot15=150\) gallons enter. At most \(30\) gallons may remain, so LeRoy must remove at least \(150-30=120\) gallons. His constant bailing rate must therefore be at least
\[
\frac{120}{15}=8\text{ gallons per minute}.
\]
This rate also works throughout the journey. After \(s\) minutes, where \(0\le s\le15\), the water remaining is
\[
(10-8)s=2s\le30\text{ gallons}.
\]
They arrive with exactly \(30\) gallons, which is allowed because sinking occurs only above \(30\). Hence the slowest rate is \(8\) gallons per minute, choice D.
